x: In the 'D' section Mick Hamlin and Bob Picton two of our young members who are showing plenty of improvement won their 6 mile badges. In section 'C' we saw some fine walking from Steve Laker-Jones when he finished 2nd and covered 7mls 196yds thus winning his 7 mile Badge.
In the individual handicap Dave King was 2nd and Gerry Cameron 7th, and these two with the help of Steve Laker-Jones and John Knifton won the handicap team race
Internationals Nihill and Fogg were others to come under the judges ban. Steve Laker-Jones walked well, and it was good to see Bob Barnes making a come-back after 2 years of studies.
The two mile walk saw Ray Middleton score an expected win but Steve Laker-Jones was breathing down his neck for the first few laps and looked most impressive.

For the future, JWG hopes to see Steve Laker-Jones come on this winter and do well in next year's RWA 10 miles and 20 Kilos; also to see Pat Duncan and Dave King do especially well at the longer distances--they could be two of our main hopes next year.

Throughout the majority of the race Belgrave led in the team championship, but in the closing stages the 3rd and 4th strings in the Highgate team came through strongly to pip our lads by 1 point! John Knifton walked very well to lead our team home and Steve Laker-Jones had a "blinder".

Ray middleton chased home his regular rival Nihill in the 5 miles with Ray Hall supporting well in 7th position. In the 3 miles event we really went to town with John Knifton, Steve Laker-Jones and Pat Duncan finishing 2nd, 4th, and 13th respectively.

Held on the day of our opening '5', Steve Laker-Jones and Ray Hall travelled to join our three 'local' lads, Eric Hall, Gerry Cameron, and Bob Farley (having his first outing since returning from Germany and joining Loughborough College).

Another whom we have counted on in the past is Steve Laker-Jones who is only just getting out again after two severe bouts of tonsillitis. With Mike and Steve at their best our teams would receive a boost.
Turn-outs have been disappointing this summer and some faces rarely seen Steve Laker-Jones, David Mayo and Mick Hamlin for instance. We understand the latter is shortly going abroad.
